decisions.reason: After several years, this broad dietary supplement range looks peripheral to the firm's stronger pharma and generics base, and the option value is likely largely exhausted if traction has not clearly emerged.

A skin-and-hair supplement sits in a crowded pharmacy niche with limited differentiation, so a large firm with many alternatives would likely reallocate resources once market feedback is sufficiently known.
Joint-health supplements fit pharmacy demand and an aging customer base, and the cost of keeping this consumer-health option open is still modest relative to its possible upside.

The immune supplement is relatively distinctive within the range and remains a reasonable consumer-health option to keep open because uncertainty about its longer-run demand can still justify low ongoing support costs.

This generic blood-pressure medicine is close to the firm's core capabilities in prescription products, manufacturing, quality, and regulation, so despite the earlier problem it is more likely to be retained than abandoned.

The OTC migraine triptan fits the firm's stated portfolio-broadening strategy and pharmacy relationships, so management would likely continue it while exploiting the option to build a stronger consumer-health position.
